name: Harlem Renaissance
title: The story of the Harlem Renaissance

text: More than 100 years ago, many African Americans moved from the South to cities in the North, looking for a better life.
Many settled in Harlem, in New York City, which became an African-American neighbourhood.
src: 1917 to 1939 (approximate) / the Great Migration carried African Americans out of the Jim Crow South to the cities of the Northeast and Midwest, in search of a better life
Many more arrived during World War I / Harlem in Manhattan, New York City / became an African-American neighbourhood in the early 1900s

text: But racism followed them north, and race riots broke out across the country.
Black soldiers came home from the war to a nation that often did not respect what they had done.
src: Yet racism followed them north / race riots broke out across the country in the Red Summer of 1919
Black soldiers of segregated units such as the Harlem Hellfighters came home to a nation that often did not respect their accomplishments

text: Black writers, artists and thinkers such as W. E. B. Du Bois wanted to fight racism with books, art and music.
The poet Langston Hughes wrote that Harlem gave people courage to be themselves “without fear or shame”.
src: through intellect and the making of literature, art and music, Black Americans would challenge pervading racism and stereotypes / W. E. B. Du Bois
Langston Hughes wrote that Harlem gave the courage “to express our individual dark-skinned selves without fear or shame”

text: A musical made by African Americans, called Shuffle Along, brought jazz to the theatres of Broadway.
Duke Ellington and Louis Armstrong led bands, and the sculptor Augusta Savage made art about everyday Black people.
src: In 1921 Shuffle Along, written, composed and produced by African Americans, brought jazz to Broadway
Duke Ellington, Louis Armstrong and Fletcher Henderson led bands / Augusta Savage put everyday Black people at the forefront of her sculpture

text: The movement relied a lot on rich white supporters, and it ended suddenly when the hard times of the Great Depression came.
Its pride and courage helped prepare the way for the civil rights movement that came later.
src: it depended heavily on white patrons and publishers, and it ended abruptly in the Great Depression
helped lay the foundation for the civil rights movement after World War II, giving the African-American community a spirit of self-determination
